items.title: Stand up the admin API boundary with its own identity domain and default-deny policy engine
items.outcome: The administrative API is a separately deployed process on its own host with its own database role, reachable only over mutually authenticated, address-restricted transport, behind an identity domain that is not the customer one, with every route evaluated by a default-deny policy engine.
items.context: Implemented literally, an administrative console makes every staff account a total-compromise vector over other people's salary and debt data. The boundary is what limits the blast radius, and it has to exist before any administrative feature does.
scope: Separate deployable process and host with its own configuration and database role
Mutual transport authentication and an address allowlist enforced at the edge
Administrative identity domain separate from customer identity, with hardware-backed second factor required
Short session lifetime and a separate cookie domain
Policy evaluation on every route, default deny, including a ticket reference in the decision input
Administrative accounts structurally cannot be customer accounts
acceptance_criteria: A request without a valid client certificate or from a non-allowlisted address is rejected at the edge
The administrative database role cannot read customer tables that the policy does not permit, proven by a direct database test
A customer credential cannot authenticate to the administrative domain and the reverse is also true
A route added without a policy decision fails the coverage check and the build
Sessions expire within the published limit and expiry takes effect mid-session
Every policy decision, allow or deny, writes an audit event
contracts_schema: Implements the administrative contract published separately from the customer contract
security_privacy: The administrative process never receives raw data encryption keys
Policy input includes actor, action, resource, justification and ticket reference
observability: Publishes decision counts by outcome and by route, and alerts on a deny spike
tests: Edge rejection tests for certificate and address
Policy coverage check with a planted uncovered route
rollout_rollback: Deployed to an internal environment first with no production data; production enablement requires the audit chain to be live
Rollback removes the administrative host from the edge, which fully disables the surface
non_goals: Console user interface, which is a separate ticket
Feature-specific administrative capabilities
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the administrative module, its deployment manifest and policy definitions. The admin repository consumes the published administrative contract only.

items.title: Implement the tamper-evident administrative audit chain and write-once stream
items.outcome: Every administrative action is written to a hash-chained, append-only record and streamed to storage that administrators cannot delete from, with a verification job that fails loudly if the chain is broken.
items.context: Administrative controls without an unfalsifiable record are decorative: the actions that matter most are exactly the ones a malicious operator would remove. The chain has to land before any unmasking, elevation or support tooling exists, or those actions happen unattributably.
scope: Hash chaining where each record commits to the previous record and its content
Insert-only grants so no role can update or delete a record
Continuous streaming to write-once storage outside the administrative blast radius
Scheduled chain verification with alerting on a break
Recovery procedure for a legitimate chain discontinuity such as a restore
acceptance_criteria: An attempted update or delete fails at the database level
Modifying a stored record breaks verification and raises an alert within the published interval
The streamed copy is retained under an immutability policy and the administrative role cannot delete it
Verification runs on a schedule and its result is visible without running it manually
A restore-induced discontinuity is distinguishable from tampering and follows the documented procedure
Chain records contain no monetary values or unmasked personal data
contracts_schema: Extends the audit event schema with the chaining fields; consumers read the same shape
security_privacy: Immutability is enforced by storage policy, not only by application code
The verification job runs with credentials the administrative process does not hold
observability: Publishes verification result, chain length and last verified position
tests: Tamper detection test with a modified record
rollout_rollback: Enabled before any administrative feature is exposed; the administrative surface stays disabled until verification is green
Rollback is not applicable; disabling the chain disables the administrative surface
non_goals: Behavioural monitoring, which is a separate ticket
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the chain implementation and verification job. Storage immutability configuration is coordinated with infra but owned here as policy.

items.title: Implement server-side redaction and independently sourced unmask authorization
items.outcome: Financial fields are redacted server-side by default, and unmasking requires an independently sourced, eligible access basis plus a recorded purpose and distinct approval, with deny as the failure mode.
items.context: A support ticket created by the operator who wants access is not independent authorization. Redaction and provenance-checked unmasking land together; elevation, bulk-export gating and monitoring remain separate controls with different failure modes and reviewers.
scope: Server-side redaction so unmasked values never cross the wire by default
Unmask operation requiring an eligible user-originated support request, system-originated security incident or statutory request, plus recorded purpose and distinct approval
Immutable originator, source channel and provenance class on every access-basis record; operator-originated support records are never eligible
Deny-by-default behaviour when the ticket system is unreachable
Notification to the affected user when their detail-level records are accessed
acceptance_criteria: An administrative response contains only masked values unless an approved unmask applies, proven at the interface level
An unmask request with a closed, invalid, operator-originated, self-approved or unreachable access basis is denied; the failure mode is deny
The requesting operator cannot create or change the record that authorizes the read and cannot serve as its approver
The affected user is notified within the published window and the notification contains no operator identity where policy forbids it
Operators never receive raw data encryption keys; the redaction service is the only read path
contracts_schema: Implements the administrative contract in which masked representation is the default and unmask is a distinct operation
security_privacy: Purpose, provenance class, immutable source reference and distinct approver are mandatory policy inputs and are recorded in the chain
Operators never receive raw data encryption keys; the redaction service is the only read path
observability: Publishes unmask counts and denials per operator
tests: Operator-created ticket, forged provenance and requester-as-approver denial tests
Static and runtime assertion that no administrative path unwraps a key
rollout_rollback: Enabled only after the audit chain is verified green; redaction and unmask are individually flagged
Rollback tightens rather than loosens: disabling unmask leaves everything masked
non_goals: Elevation, bulk-export gating and access monitoring, which are their own ticket
Console user interface, which is a separate ticket
Customer-facing access transparency, which belongs to E16
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the redaction service and unmask policy. Support, incident and statutory systems provide immutable provenance through narrow verification interfaces and are never read as free-form justification.

items.title: Implement just-in-time elevation, four-eyes bulk export and access monitoring
items.outcome: Elevation is time-boxed and needs a distinct second approver, bulk export has no single-actor path, break-glass use is recorded and rotated, and unusual access patterns are blocked rather than merely logged.
items.context: Elevation without a second approver is self-service and monitoring without blocking is a post-incident report. These controls share one failure mode - a single motivated operator - and are grouped so they are reviewed as one control set on top of the redaction boundary.
scope: Just-in-time elevation with a maximum duration, automatic expiry and a distinct second approver
Bulk export gated behind a formal request with dual approval and full recording
Formal access-basis provenance that cannot be originated or rewritten by either approving operator
Break-glass account with vaulted credentials, dual presence, session recording and automatic rotation after use
Behavioural monitoring for bulk retrieval, out-of-scope access and unusual time or origin, with blocking rather than alerting alone
Administrative security notices to an affected user are enqueued through the T-NOT-01 outbox under the payload allowlist, so no administrative message can carry financial detail
acceptance_criteria: Self-approval of elevation is impossible and expiry revokes access mid-session
No single-actor bulk export path exists; an attempted bypass is blocked and alerted
A simulated malicious operator retrieving many records is blocked and an alert reaches the on-call owner
Break-glass use rotates the credential automatically and leaves a recording
The second approver is a distinct qualified reviewer under T-GOV-03; where none exists, elevation and bulk export stay disabled rather than degraded
The requestor, access-basis originator and second approver satisfy separation-of-duties policy; a conflict denies before any elevated session is issued
contracts_schema: Implements the administrative contract elevation and export request shapes, including the second-approver field
security_privacy: Elevation and export approvals are recorded in the audit chain with both actor identities
A blocked monitoring event stops the request rather than recording it after the fact
observability: Publishes elevation grants, denials, export requests and monitoring blocks per operator
tests: Dual-approval bulk export bypass attempt test
Operator-originated basis and separation-of-duties conflict tests
rollout_rollback: Each control is individually flagged so one can be tightened without redeploying the rest
Rollback tightens rather than loosens: disabling a control disables the feature it protects
non_goals: Redaction and unmasking, which are their own ticket
Console user interface, which is a separate ticket
Customer-facing access transparency, which belongs to E16
Notification delivery, scheduling, preferences and provider integration, which T-NOT-01 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns elevation, export gating, break-glass and monitoring. It builds on the redaction boundary rather than reimplementing it.

items.title: Build the admin console shell, operator session and default-deny navigation
items.outcome: As an operator, I sign in to a console on its own authentication domain and see only the areas my role permits, with every screen defaulting to no access rather than to a financial browser.
items.context: The console is where the administrative boundary becomes a product. If it presents a searchable financial browser, every control behind it is irrelevant. The shell decides that: it owns the operator session, the navigation, the redaction defaults and the absence of any per-user financial listing route. The capability screens are separate tickets that mount inside it, so each can be built, reviewed and shipped independently rather than arriving as one unreviewable change.
scope: Operator sign-in on the separate authentication domain, with session lifetime, idle timeout and revocation
Navigation and route registration where a route absent from the operator's role is not rendered and not reachable
The shared redacted presentation primitive that every capability screen composes, so redaction is the default rather than a per-screen decision
The confirmation primitive that destructive and configuration actions reuse, recording before and after values through the administrative API
The structural absence of any route that lists an individual user's transactions or balances
The shell into which the plan, provider, support, analytics and audit screens mount
acceptance_criteria: An operator session is issued only by the administrative authentication domain and a customer session is rejected
A route absent from the operator's role is neither rendered in navigation nor reachable by direct address
No screen in the console lists an individual user's transactions or balances; the capability does not exist to be misused, verified by an absence test over the route table
Every monetary or personal field rendered through the shared primitive is redacted unless an unmasking grant is present
The confirmation primitive records old and new values through the administrative API before the change is applied, not after
Idle timeout and revocation end the session within the published time, verified rather than configured
The console never calls the customer API, verified by a network assertion in the end-to-end run
contracts_schema: Consumes the published administrative contract only; the console never calls the customer API
security_privacy: The console holds no credentials beyond the operator session and never sees key material
Redaction is a property of the shared primitive, so a new screen is redacted by default and un-redacting is an explicit, reviewable act
observability: Publishes operator action counts by type and session lifecycle events, which the capability screens extend rather than redefine
tests: Absence test proving no per-user financial listing route exists in the route table
Cross-domain test asserting a customer session cannot authenticate to the console
Role-based route reachability test including direct address
Redaction default test over the shared primitive
Confirmation ordering test asserting the record precedes the change
Network assertion that no request reaches the customer API
rollout_rollback: Released to a named operator group first; no capability screen mounts until the shell's absence and redaction tests are green
Rollback removes console access without affecting the administrative API or its records
non_goals: Administrative authorization mechanics, which the api tickets own
Plan, feature and quota management, which T-ADM-07 owns
Provider configuration and spend caps, which T-ADM-08 owns
Support tooling, which T-ADM-09 owns
Aggregate analytics, which T-ADM-10 owns
Audit review and the operator red-team suite, which T-ADM-11 and T-ADM-12 own
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo admin. Owns the shell, the operator session, the navigation contract and the shared redaction and confirmation primitives. The five capability tickets mount into it and extend its telemetry rather than redefining any of them. All enforcement lives behind the administrative API.

items.title: Build user support intake, status and the ticket-verification endpoint
items.outcome: A user can raise a support request, attach privacy-safe evidence, and track its status against a published response target, and an administrator can only unmask data for a request that this service confirms exists and is open for that user.
items.context: Support is referenced by the admin console, the trust surfaces, the billing flows and the onboarding help links, and it exists nowhere. That is a security problem as much as a product gap: the four-eyes and unmasking controls in E13 are justified by an approved support request, and if support requests live in an unowned mailbox then the justification is unverifiable and the control is decoration. It is also where diagnostics arrive, which is exactly where raw financial data leaks if nobody defines what may be attached.
scope: Support request creation, category, status transitions, threaded messages and resolution
Attachment intake with type and size limits, scanning, expiry, and a redaction rule for what may be attached
Diagnostic bundle collection that is opt-in per request and carries a declared, allowlisted field set
Vendor adapter so an external helpdesk can be adopted without changing the intake or the verification contract
Ticket-verification endpoint the admin console calls before any unmask or elevated read, returning existence, ownership and open state
Immutable request provenance: user-originated, system-originated incident or operator-originated, with source channel and originator recorded at creation
Eligibility response that excludes operator-originated records from unmask authorization regardless of category or later reassignment
Response-target policy per category, and the priority-support entitlement that changes it
Escalation and breach handling when a response target is missed
acceptance_criteria: A user can create a request, see its status and its response target, and add messages to it until it is resolved
An attachment outside the allowed types or above the size limit is refused, and every attachment expires at the declared time and is then unreadable
A diagnostic bundle contains only allowlisted fields, proven by a test with a planted monetary amount and a planted merchant name that both fail the check

The verification endpoint returns whether a ticket exists, whether it belongs to the named user, whether it is open, its immutable provenance class and whether that class is eligible, and returns no free-form content
An operator-created or operator-converted request is ineligible for unmasking even when open and assigned to another operator
An unmask attempt in the admin console with no verifiable open ticket for that user is refused, proven by an end-to-end test against the admin path
A verification result cannot be replayed to justify a second unmask outside the published window
The priority-support entitlement changes the response target and nothing else, and a user without it sees the standard target
Missing a response target raises an escalation that is visible without opening the helpdesk
Swapping the vendor adapter changes no intake shape and no verification behaviour, demonstrated with a second adapter in tests
contracts_schema: Implements the support request, status, thread and attachment shapes published by T-CON-11
Publishes the ticket-verification contract as its own narrow interface: existence, ownership, open state, immutable provenance class and eligibility, with no free-form content
security_privacy: The verification endpoint is a control surface: it is authenticated as the admin service, rate limited, fully audited, and returns no ticket content
Support staff read redacted data by default; unmasking is the E13 path and always requires an open verified ticket plus the four-eyes control
Attachments and diagnostics are covered by the erasure path, so a resolved request does not become a permanent copy of a user's data outside the erasure boundary
No support surface accepts or displays credentials, session tokens or recovery codes, and a message containing one is rejected rather than stored
observability: Open request count, age distribution, response-target breaches and unmask verifications are all recorded
An unusual rate of verification calls from the admin service raises an alert, because that is what a fishing expedition looks like
tests: Attachment type, size and expiry tests
Diagnostic allowlist test with planted financial fields
Verification endpoint contract test proving no ticket content is returned
End-to-end refusal test: unmask without an open verified ticket
Operator-originated request remains ineligible across reassignment, category change and reopen tests
rollout_rollback: Intake and status ship first with a single category, then verification is enabled and only afterwards does the admin console begin to require it
Rollback disables intake and leaves existing requests readable; the admin unmask path fails closed if verification is unavailable, which is the intended direction
non_goals: Admin console operator screens, which T-ADM-04 and the T-ADM-07 to T-ADM-11 capability tickets own
Client support surfaces, which T-SUP-02 and T-SUP-03 own
Building a helpdesk product: the vendor adapter exists so we do not
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns intake, status, attachments, the vendor adapter and the verification endpoint. The admin console consumes verification and never reads the support store directly; the clients consume the published contract.

items.title: Implement administrator joiner, mover and leaver lifecycle with recertification
items.outcome: Administrative access is granted, changed and removed through a defined lifecycle: a hardware factor is required to hold it, approver eligibility is enforced, a role change revokes what it should, access is recertified on a schedule, and offboarding produces evidence that every path is closed.
items.context: E13 designs strong controls for what an administrator may do and says nothing about how someone becomes one, stops being one, or is periodically confirmed to still need it. Insider risk is not primarily about a malicious action inside a session; it is about an account that should have been closed three months ago still working. The four-eyes control also silently degrades if the second approver is someone who should no longer be eligible.
scope: Joiner: request, approval, role assignment, hardware factor enrolment before first privileged action
Mover: role change that removes the permissions of the previous role rather than accumulating them
Leaver: offboarding that revokes sessions, tokens, database roles, break-glass credentials and console access, with evidence
Approver eligibility rules, so the second pair of eyes cannot be an ineligible or departed account
Periodic recertification of every administrative account and every standing permission, with automatic removal when it lapses
Break-glass account handling: how it is created, stored, used, rotated after use and reviewed
Separation of administrative identity from customer identity, enforced rather than assumed
acceptance_criteria: An administrative account cannot perform a privileged action before a hardware factor is enrolled, proven by a test
A role change removes the previous role's permissions in the same operation; a test asserts the old permission no longer resolves
Offboarding revokes sessions, refresh families, database role membership, console access and break-glass eligibility, and produces an evidence record naming each
An approval by an ineligible or offboarded account is refused, proven by a test that offboards the approver mid-flow
A permission that is not recertified within the published window is removed automatically, and the removal is audited
Break-glass use triggers an alert, is time-bounded, and forces a credential rotation afterwards, proven by a drill
An administrative identity cannot be the same principal as a customer identity, enforced at enrolment rather than by convention
Every lifecycle event is written to the administrative audit stream defined by T-ADR-ADMIN-06
contracts_schema: Publishes the administrative account lifecycle states and the recertification record as machine-readable data the console and the audit stream both read
security_privacy: Lifecycle actions are themselves privileged and subject to the same four-eyes control as the actions they grant
No lifecycle record contains customer data; it references accounts and permissions only
Offboarding evidence is retained under the administrative audit retention rule, not deleted with the account
observability: Count of administrative accounts, standing permissions, overdue recertifications and break-glass uses are all reported
An overdue recertification and any break-glass use raise alerts
rollout_rollback: Applied to the existing administrative accounts before the console gains any unmask capability, so the lifecycle exists before the privilege does
Rollback would restore standing access, which is why the rollback position is documented as a temporary exception with an expiry rather than an open-ended revert
non_goals: Customer identity, authentication and recovery, which E03 owns
Console screens, which T-ADM-04 and the T-ADM-07 to T-ADM-11 capability tickets own
Hiring, contracting and human resources process
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the administrative account lifecycle, approver eligibility and recertification. The console surfaces these states and the audit stream records them; neither reimplements the rules.
